svg.text: Before (Fig 10.1): all users depend on OPS
Before: User1 uses only op1 but, in a language like Java, its source inadvertently depends on op2 and op3; a change to op2 in OPS forces User1 to be recompiled and
redeployed though nothing it cares about changed. After: User1 depends on U1Ops and op1 only, not OPS, so an unrelated change to OPS does not recompile or redeploy
static languages (Java) force declarations users must import or use, creating
source dependencies that force recompilation; dynamic ones (Ruby, Python) infer at
runtime: more flexible, less coupled systems
But it is deeper than language
it is harmful to depend on modules that contain more than you need, in source code
